key_insight: Iterative strong coupling stabilizes FD-SPH simulations of lightweight floating rigid bodies where single-pass coupling fails, even with drastic time-step reduction.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports simulation of lightweight and complex floating bodies in transient free-surface flows without explicit interface reconstruction or surface-normal evaluation.
method: Combine volume-based hydrodynamic loads with Newton–Euler rigid-body updates.
Iteratively correct the velocity mismatch between pressure-projected fictitious fluid and rigid bodies within each time step.
Use a fractional-step interpretation to identify conditions for equivalent PMS projection and Newton–Euler velocities.
evidence_signal: Iterative coupling remained stable for tested cube specific gravities of 0.1–1.0, while settling-disk and dam-break benchmarks agreed with published results and experimental trends.
watch_item: Strong coupling requires repeated updates within each time step; all production runs met the residual criterion, but the abstract does not quantify computational overhead.
paper_title: Partitioned iterative FD-SPH for fluid-rigid-body interaction: Stability and validation for lightweight floating bodies
